abstract:
Accurate molecular property prediction (MPP) remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Given the limited availability of labeled molecular data, multimodal molecular representation learning offers a promising means of integrating complementary structural information for MPP. Existing multimodal models still face two limitations: (i) common fusion strategies, particularly direct concatenation, can introduce redundant information or signals that are weakly relevant to the target property; and (ii) the effective incorporation of complementary physicochemical priors into multimodal representations remains insufficiently explored.
Here, we proposed ReMoD-Mol, a reliability-aware multimodal framework that integrated molecular graphs, SMILES sequences and two-dimensional molecular images. Task-adaptive modality calibration learned one set of weights per benchmark from downstream supervision to regulate the relative contributions of the three molecular views. Descriptor- and fingerprint-based teachers further provided task-conditioned chemical priors through train-only, five-fold out-of-fold knowledge distillation. Prototype-guided embedding shaping together with graph-view and SMILES-view consistency objectives regularized the fused representation space. Across nine MoleculeNet benchmark datasets spanning regression and classification, ReMoD-Mol achieved the best mean performance on seven datasets and the second-best on the other two in a scaffold-split comparison with 14 baselines. Representation analyses revealed smoother property-related manifolds and more discriminative class structures, while learned modality coefficients exhibited distinct task-dependent fusion patterns. Teacher-prior and ablation analyses further supported the complementary roles of chemical-prior transfer and multi-view representation regularization.
Source code, processed datasets and implementation details are publicly available at https://github.com/27167199/ReMoD-Mol.
